tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

pipeline-scope-abstract: Abstract p.1 states the three-stage pipeline and the five-qubit QsRF as the paper's own method; Sections II-A to II-D match.
qubo-formulation-definition: Section II-C(a), Eq. (3), p.3 defines the mask z, k=5, Ktop=20, penalty mu about 10^3 and Q = -diag(w) + mu 11^T.
algorithm1-qubo-differs: Both forms are the paper's own: Section II-C(a) gives -diag(w)+mu 11^T, Algorithm 1 line 13 gives w w^T + mu I. The paper states both, so the value records a real internal inconsistency.
importance-score-definition: Section II-B, Eq. (2), p.3 defines delta_u(j), the 20% bootstrap average w_j and the Ktop=20 candidate set.
qaoa-configuration: Section II-C(b) p.3 gives p=3, SPSA, 128 shots; Algorithm 1 line 14 gives 200 shots. Both are the paper's own setup statements and they differ.
qaoa-fallback-top-k: Section II-C(b) p.3 defines the acceptance rule and the top-k fallback by w_j.
qsrf-definition: Section II-D p.3 defines the bagged tree ensemble, the bootstrap with feature-index perturbation and the mean over tree outputs.
tree-count-inconsistent: Section I-B item 3 p.2 says 100 trees (10 runs x 10 trees); Section II-D p.3 says T = 200. Section II-F says 100 depth-8 trees. The paper states both numbers.
dictionary-learning-setup: Section II-A(b),(c) p.3: K=50 clusters, A=20 atoms per cluster, union is 1000 atoms (50 x 20).
dataset-statistics: Table I p.4 read in context: columns are Users, Items, Interactions, Tags, Sparsity for ICM-150 then ICM-500; the values match the item.
split-and-protocol: Section II-G p.4 states the 80/20 user-stratified split, the further 80/20 split, 64:16:20 and five seeds.
future-work-and-limits: Section V p.7 lists the three avenues as future work, which marks what the paper leaves out. The value states only that they list them.
qsrf-simulator-only: Section II-F p.4 and the Section V implementation note p.7 both state that all runs used the PennyLane simulator, noise-free, with hardware deferred.
review-scope-ai-for-quantum: Section 1 p.4 states the review covers AI for quantum only and excludes quantum for AI, referring to Ref. [18].
review-aim-abstract: Abstract p.2 states the review's aim and its span from device design to applications.
parameter-transfer-definition: Section 3.2 p.11: 'Parameter transfer is the process of ...' is the paper's own uncited definition.
control-tuning-optimization-definitions: Section 4 pp.12-13 defines control, tuning and optimization in its opening paragraph, uncited.
pptnqfe-simulator-only: Section 1.3 p.2 states all quantum computations used a state vector simulator; Section 5.2 p.9 repeats it for regression.
pptnqfe-hat-basis-setup: Section 2 p.3 states the 1D basis on [-1,1] of piecewise linear hat functions, with node placement per section.
pptnqfe-locality-sparse: Section 2 p.3 states property (II) (local support) and that it leads to sparse vectors, and that (III) is beneficial but not mandatory. These are the paper's own requirements on the basis.
pptnqfe-two-nonzero-entries: Section 4 p.5: a property of the paper's own hat basis vector Phi(x), which follows directly from its defined construction.
pptnqfe-rank2-two-qubit-gates: Section 4 p.6 gives the explicit MPS cores with maximum rank 2, and Section 3 p.5 states that this needs only 2-qubit gates. It describes the paper's own construction.
pptnqfe-loads-basis-not-function: Remark 4.1 p.6 states what the paper's embedding loads (the basis set at a point) as against a single function. The value does not assert anything about the cited works beyond that contrast.
pptnqfe-regression-training-setup: Section 5.2 p.9 states the simulator, AMSGrad, MSE and 50 equally spaced points.
pptnqfe-overparam-by-design: Section 5.2 p.11 states the parameter counts were deliberately larger than needed to show noise overfitting.
pptnqfe-mps-variational-heuristic: Section 5.2 p.11: the paper itself says the MPS-structured variational layer 'remains a heuristic approach at this stage'.
pptnqfe-open-circuit-design: Section 5.2 p.12 and Section 6 p.13 state the circuit-design question as open, about the paper's own method.
pptnqfe-kernel-setup: Section 5.3 p.12 and the Figure 10 caption give 6 qubits, 13 frequencies per feature (169), 8 hat functions per feature (64) and the 80% random training set.
pptnqfe-toy-examples-scope: Section 1.3 p.2 states the toy-example scope of the paper, with its own results in Section 5.
pptnqfe-no-qa: Section 1.3 p.2 states the embeddings are not inherently superior and confer no QA; Section 5.2 p.9 repeats it. A caveat about its own work.
pptnqfe-noise-overhead-limit: Section 6 pp.12-13 states gate-conversion overhead and that statistical and hardware noise were not explored.
m-definition: Section 3 p.7 defines phi as the max |q_ij| and M = phi * C(r,2).
lemma-1-1flip-local-opt: Lemma 1 p.7 is stated with its 1-flip local optimality condition (5) and proved in two lines from (5).
lemma-2-pair-sum-bound: Lemma 2 p.7 is stated and proved: each pair term is +/- q_ij, there are C(r,2) of them, so the sum is at most M.
proposition-1-sum-below-m: Proposition 1 pp.8-9 is stated with its conditions (1-flip local optimum, improving r-flip) and proved from the strict inequality (16) and Lemma 2.
table-1-instances: Section 3 p.11 states the instance filter: up to 38 instances, 2500 to 6000 variables.
algorithms-compared-setup: Section 4 p.12 states Algorithms 3, 4, 5 with r=2 were compared, and the best was then compared to MST2.
mst2-parameters: Section 4 p.12 states MST2 default parameters, 25,000 x size then 10,000 x size iterations.
hardware-setup: Section 4 p.12 states the single-core Xeon E5420, 8 GB, 2.5 GHz, GNU C++ 4.8.5, Open PBS.
large-instance-setup: Section 4 pp.12-13 states the 30,000-variable high-density instances, 600 s limit and r=2.
stopping-criterion: Section 4 p.13 states that the CPU limit for Algorithm 5 was checked before starting a tabu search. 'Considered fair' is the authors' view, and the value says so.
limit-cost-and-tuning: Section 4 limitations paragraph, pp.17-18 states both limits about the proposed algorithms.
limit-instance-dependence: Section 4 limitations paragraph pp.17-18 states efficacy varies with instance characteristics and depends on a good 1-flip optimum.
rflip-heuristic-limits: Section 4 limitations paragraph: 'As heuristic methods, they do not guarantee finding the global optimum.'
rflip-mst2-comparison-setup: Section 4 p.12 states the D-Wave solver's Python wrapper limits and that the original MST2 C++ code was used instead.
alonso-universal-hamiltonian-family-defi: Section 2.2 p.6 states Definition 2.1 as the paper's definition, adopted from [18], with the frequency spectrum defined in the line before.
alonso-pricing-as-coefficient-sum: Section 3.1.1 p.10 gives the pricing sum of coefficient products and Section 3.2.1 p.15 computes the price from it; it is the paper's own formulation. 'Typically in closed form' is a mild aside.
alonso-three-approaches-design: Section 3.2 pp.11-14 describes the three methods and the benchmark role of Method III.
alonso-same-ansatz-both-methods: Section 3.2 p.13 and Section 4.1 p.20 state the common ansatz and the n x n configurations.
alonso-method3-mrqae-sign: Section 3.2 p.14 states Method III uses mRQAE for signed coefficients, as the paper's own method choice (details cited to [8]).
alonso-cost-proxy-circuit-runs: Section 3.2 p.14 states the evaluation protocol: circuit runs per coefficient as cost proxy.
alonso-method1-dft-extraction: Section 3.2.1 pp.14-15 states the DFT extraction and the price formula.
alonso-method2-self-supervised-risk: Section 3.2.2 pp.15-17 states the empirical CDF labels, Monte Carlo density term and boundary constraint terms. The DML remark is the authors' note.
alonso-experiment-put-option-setup: Section 4.1 pp.18-19 states the put option, S0=100, r=0.1, T=1, sigma=0.25 and K=90,100,110.
alonso-minimum-schemes: Section 4.1 p.20 states the minimum PQC schemes, 6 x 6 and 4 x 4. The 'chosen to be accurate' clause is the authors' view.
alonso-fourier-pqc-method: Abstract p.1 states what the two methods rely on; Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 carry it out.
alonso-training-randomness-limit: Section 4.2.1 p.22 states outliers from random weight initialization and the need for more repetitions with statistical analysis, about its own results.

theory_low.pptnqfe-auto-normalization: Section 4 p.5 is an inline remark, not a stated and proved result. It holds only where the hat functions form a partition of unity, and the node placement in Section 5.1 differs from Section 5.2.
theory_low.pptnqfe-diagonal-observables-polynomial: Section 5.2 p.9 reads Eq. (3) and Figure 6 for theta=0 as an inline observation. No theorem or proof, and the sign-change frequency remark is read from a figure.
theory_low.pptnqfe-term-counts: Section 5.2 p.11 is an inline count with no proof. For n=2 the stated 2^(2n-1)+2^(n-1) equals 10, the total of all products in Figure 5 (diagonal ones included), so 'non-polynomial terms' looks wrong.
theory_low.theorem-1-improving-rflip: Theorem 1 p.7-8: the printed inequality (13) is '<=' but the proof derives the strict form (15), and the quotes drop the inequality. The value's 'exactly when ... less than' follows the proof, not the stated theorem. The proof is short and uses Lemma 1.
theory_low.corollary-of-theorem-1-rflip-local-opt: Section 3 pp.8-9 labels this a corollary of Theorem 1 with no derivation written out, and it rests on Theorem 1's inequality, whose printed form disagrees with its proof.
theory_low.lemma-3-d-n-subsets: Lemma 3 p.10: the proof is one sentence ('a direct result of Proposition 1'). It only shows subsets meet the necessary condition of Proposition 1, not that a move improves, and the value's wording could be read as more.
theory_low.corollary-1-single-element: Corollary 1 pp.10-11 is stated without a derivation, and the text carries an annotation questioning its own wording. It follows from Proposition 1 but is not proved in the paper.
theory_low.alonso-cdf-quantities-not-payoff-coeffic: Section 3.1.2 p.11 is a one-clause inline remark ('it should be remarked') with no derivation.
